html: I think your question is really more about the difference between online and offline time–frequency conversion. Offline, the spectrum is an average over a stretch of time; the length of that stretch determines the frequency resolution, but since it’s offline, you choose the duration yourself. If you want to see time, you can use the short-time Fourier transform or the wavelet transform, which show time and frequency information at once. Online, the instrument probably has a buffer and computes the spectrum taking previously acquired data into account. So when you first start acquiring the signal, it can’t produce a meaningful spectrum; only as time goes on and more useful information accumulates does the spectrum become meaningful.
